title: Nonlinear functions
what_is_tested: You work with quadratic and exponential functions: evaluating \(f(x)\), reading the vertex, intercepts and growth factor, choosing a model from a table or graph, and using equivalent forms that reveal a feature. Harder questions add transformations and composition. This is the largest single skill in the Math section.
how_to_spot: The stem uses function notation such as \(f(x)\) or \(h(t)\), shows a curved graph or a table, or describes a quantity that grows or shrinks by a percent, or rises and falls like a thrown object.
method: Identify the function type: \(ax^{2} + bx + c\) is quadratic; \(a \cdot b^{x}\) is exponential.
To evaluate, substitute the input in parentheses everywhere the variable appears, then follow the order of operations.
Quadratic: vertex form \(a(x - h)^{2} + k\) shows the vertex \((h, k)\); factored form shows the \(x\)-intercepts; standard form shows the \(y\)-intercept \(c\).
Exponential \(a \cdot b^{t}\): \(a\) is the starting value; \(b > 1\) is growth by \((b - 1) \cdot 100\%\), \(b < 1\) is decay by \((1 - b) \cdot 100\%\).
For transformations, \(f(x - h)\) moves the graph right \(h\) units and \(f(x) + k\) moves it up \(k\) units.
pitfalls: Multiplying before applying the exponent, e.g. treating \(5 \cdot 2^{3}\) as \(10^{3}\) (arithmetic).
Reading the growth factor \(1.03\) as a \(1.03\%\) or \(103\%\) increase instead of \(3\%\) (concept).
Getting the shift direction backward: \(f(x + 1)\) moves the graph left, not right (sign_error).
Giving the time of the maximum when the question asks for the maximum height, or the reverse (wrong_quantity).
Checking only the first two rows of a table, so a linear model looks as good as an exponential one (wrong_formula).
calculator: In the Graph tab, type the function and tap the curve to read the vertex, the intercepts, or a value; this is often the fastest route for maximum and minimum questions. For "which form is equivalent" questions, graph two forms and see whether they match.

cards.title: Foundations: evaluate and read a function
steps: Replace the variable with the given input, in parentheses.
Apply exponents first, then multiply, then add or subtract.
In a model \(a \cdot b^{t}\), name \(a\) (the start) and \(b\) (the factor per time unit).
Answer what is asked: an output value, an input, or what a number means.

worked_example.stem: The function \(p\) is defined by \(p(x) = 5 \cdot 2^{x} - 3\). What is the value of \(p(3)\)?
walkthrough: Then multiply and subtract: \(5 \cdot 8 - 3 = 40 - 3 = 37\), choice B.
Choice D comes from multiplying \(5 \cdot 2 = 10\) first and computing \(10^{3} - 3\); choice C forgets to subtract 3.
worked_example.verify:
x = symbols('x')
p = 5*2**x - 3
assert value(choices[answer]) == p.subs(x, 3) == 37
assert all(value(choices[k]) != 37 for k in choices if k != answer)

cards.title: Medium: vertex, maximum and intercepts of a quadratic
steps: Decide which feature is asked: the vertex (maximum or minimum) or a zero (where the output is \(0\)).
For the vertex of \(ax^{2} + bx + c\), use \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), or read \((h, k)\) from vertex form.
Substitute that \(x\) into the function to get the maximum or minimum value; for a zero, solve \(f(x) = 0\).
Check the units and pick the value that fits (time cannot be negative).

worked_example.stem: A small model rocket is launched from a platform. Its height above the ground, in meters, \(t\) seconds after launch is given by \(h(t) = -5t^{2} + 30t + 35\). What is the maximum height of the rocket, in meters?
walkthrough: The maximum of a downward-opening parabola is at its vertex. Here \(a = -5\) and \(b = 30\).
Calculator route (Graph tab): graph \(y = -5x^{2} + 30x + 35\) and tap the top of the curve to see \((3, 80)\).
Do not type 3: that is the time of the maximum, not the height.
worked_example.verify:
t = symbols('t')
h = -5*t**2 + 30*t + 35
tv = solve(diff(h, t), t)
assert tv == [3]
assert Rational(spr_answers[0]) == h.subs(t, tv[0]) == 80

cards.title: Advanced: choose a model and rewrite to reveal a feature
steps: From a table, compare differences (constant means linear) and ratios (constant means exponential).
Write the model as \(a \cdot b^{t}\) with \(a\) the starting value and \(b\) the ratio per step.
Use exponent rules to change the time unit: \(b^{t} = (\sqrt{b})^{2t}\) for half-years, \((b^{\frac{1}{12}})^{12t}\) for months.
Pick the form that shows the requested feature, and check it equals the original at a value such as \(t = 1\).

worked_example.stem: The value, in dollars, of a printing machine \(t\) years after it was bought is modeled by \(V(t) = 18{,}000(0.81)^{t}\). Which of the following equivalent expressions shows the percent decrease in the machine's value every half-year?
walkthrough: In \(t\) years there are \(2t\) half-years, so you want the form \(18{,}000(c)^{2t}\), where \(c\) is the factor per half-year.
So \(V(t) = 18{,}000(0.9)^{2t}\), choice D: the value keeps \(90\%\) each half-year, a \(10\%\) decrease.
Choice B halves the factor instead of taking its square root; \(0.405^{2}\) is not \(0.81\), so B is not equivalent.
worked_example.verify:
t = symbols('t')
V = 18000*Rational(81, 100)**t
same = lambda k: all(value(choices[k]).subs(t, s) == V.subs(t, s) for s in [0, 1, 2, Rational(1, 2)])
assert same(answer)
assert all(not same(k) for k in choices if k != answer)
assert '0.9)^{2t}' in choices[answer]

cards.title: Challenge: transformations and combined functions
steps: Translate each description into function notation: left \(h\) means \(x + h\) inside; down \(k\) means \(- k\) outside.
Write the new function completely before substituting anything.
Set up the equation the question gives (such as \(g(k) = 29\)) and simplify to a familiar form.
Solve, then check by substituting your answer back into the new function.

worked_example.stem: The graph of \(y = g(x)\) is the result of shifting the graph of \(y = 2^{x}\) left 1 unit and down 3 units. If \(g(k) = 29\), what is the value of \(k\)?
walkthrough: Left 1 unit replaces \(x\) with \(x + 1\); down 3 units subtracts 3. So \(g(x) = 2^{x + 1} - 3\).
Choice C comes from shifting right instead of left, \(2^{k - 1} = 32\); choice B stops at \(k + 1 = 5\).
worked_example.verify:
x, k = symbols('x k')
g = 2**(x + 1) - 3
ks = solve(Eq(g.subs(x, k), 29), k)
assert ks == [4]
assert value(choices[answer]) == ks[0]
assert all(value(choices[k2]) != 4 for k2 in choices if k2 != answer)
